observationsNotFindings.observation: The repair route is NOT the one CLAUDE-G03-V1-SF1 named, and on assessment it is the better one.
observationsNotFindings.detail: My finding said the repair was to 'Add the parentReview object the v3 extraction already contains' to the G03 v1 occupancy file. That is impossible in place: v1 is frozen at 0444 and editing a reviewed artifact is forbidden. v4 instead moves the parent's own promise to a successor that carries the pin, which addresses the finding's stated 'whyItMatters' directly — I had written that 'the better-provenanced extraction, which does carry parentReview, sits at a path nobody is promised.' After v4, the promised path is the one that carries the pin.
observationsNotFindings.whyItIsRight: It also repairs the structure rather than the symptom, and it does so in the parent, which is the only artifact with authority over the promise. Contrast the sibling G01 lineage, where a v3 extraction was created at an unpromised path while claiming to occupy the promise — the defect I raised as CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1. This is the correct pattern and could be applied there.

observationsNotFindings.observation: The repair is a matched pair, and at this instant the D-086 promise points at a file with no verdict.
observationsNotFindings.detail: Parent v4 retargets to harness.DR-G03.core-startup.v4.json, which pins parent v4 in return. Both are AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW. Before the retarget the promise pointed at G03 v1, which carries a REJECT; after it, the promise points at a file that is dispatched for review — its review prompt exists, dated 07:53 — but not yet reviewed.
observationsNotFindings.whyNotAFinding: The transient is inherent to any promise-retarget and is strictly better than pointing at a rejected file whose defect cannot be repaired in place. Both halves disclose their own standing honestly and neither claims a review it does not have. Recorded so you can sequence the two acceptances rather than be surprised by the interval.

observationsNotFindings.observation: d006UnitStanding is the strongest block in the artifact and should survive any future revision verbatim.

D-006 does not define MB as 1e6 or 2^20', explicitly refuses to borrow D-102's GiB definition because that is scoped to RAM matching, holds G02 tree accounting UNDECIDED, and defers pass/fail to a later unit successor so a job can record raw bytes without claiming a comparison. That is the correct shape for an undecided unit, and it independently corroborates my earlier repo-wide measurement that no MB-to-bytes definition exists anywhere in COORD or docs/v2/architecture.

The second is inside the UNDECIDED statement itself, distinguishing D-102's GiB-as-bytes/1024^3 from these thresholds. Recorded so a later mechanical check does not misfire on them, and so that a reviewer who greps rather than reads does not raise a false finding.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: This subject both pins my verdict on its predecessor and claims to land my finding, so I ran the diff before reading the artifact's account of itself. The change surface is exactly what the dispatch permits and nothing more: zero leaf paths removed, seven added — the lands array and the predecessorV3 block with its review pin — and five values changed, of which four are identity and prose. The fifth is the only change inside any harness object in the file: G03's artifactPathWhenAuthored. G01, G02, G04 and G05 are IDENTICAL to v3 by object equality, G03 differs in exactly one key with all measurement content untouched, and the row count stays five with the same ids. The decisive test was whether the retarget points at something real that does what my finding demanded, because a retarget to nothing would leave the D-086 promise unoccupied. It does: harness.DR-G03.core-startup.v4.json exists at 0444, its own artifactPathWhenAuthored equals its own path so the new promise is self-consistent, its harness object equals this subject's G03 entry, and it carries the parentReview object — path, digest 3f2146ec, standing — whose absence was the whole substance of CLAUDE-G03-V1-SF1. Its verdict string is carefully honest about the chicken-and-egg the retarget creates: it attributes the ACCEPT to the v3 CONTENT and discloses that v4 is itself awaiting review, rather than claiming a review it does not have. Worth saying plainly: the repair route is not the one I named. I had said to add the parentReview object to the v1 occupancy file, which is impossible because v1 is frozen at 0444. Moving the parent's promise to a successor that carries the pin is the better fix, and it answers my finding's own 'whyItMatters' — that the better-provenanced extraction sat at a path nobody was promised. It is also the pattern the sibling G01 lineage should have used, where instead a v3 extraction was created at an unpromised path while claiming to occupy the promise, which is my open CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1. On the prohibitions: the two binary constants present, 26214400 and 83886080, each occur twice and every occurrence is a negation, inside G01 and G02 objects the diff proves byte-identical to reviewed v3. I checked the two 1024 hits rather than counting them — one is a /proc VmRSS kB-to-bytes measurement primitive, the other sits inside the sentence refusing to borrow D-102's GiB — and I record them because a naive sweep would flag both. d006UnitStanding holds byteMeaning UNDECIDED with explicit reasoning and defers pass/fail to a later unit successor, which corroborates my earlier repo-wide measurement that no MB conversion exists anywhere. OBL-2 is refuted by the artifact's own structure: whatThisCloses.leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded is an EMPTY ARRAY, gates2and3HoldForDR101 is false, and all five OBL-2 mentions state non-closure. Rust appears only in two negations, the lowercase hits are inside 'trust', and ceremony and notarization tokens do not occur at all. Every one of the eight 64-hex strings in the file resolves to a real file on disk — I indexed the whole docs tree rather than checking only the labelled ones — and every labelled digest matches live. v3 is unmoved, HEAD is 5d5d778, required-now is 26 across thirty gate rows, and git reports zero modified tracked files. Seventeen attacks run, seventeen refuted, zero findings. One sequencing note rather than a defect: the repair is a matched pair, so between now and the acceptance of harness.DR-G03.core-startup.v4 the D-086 promise points at a dispatched but unreviewed file. That is strictly better than pointing at a rejected one, and both halves disclose their own standing, but you may want to sequence the two acceptances together.
